definitions.meaning: a pounding is a kneading rub given to sore muscles
a therapeutic rub administered by a masseur

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a pound will buy at a clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur's work is both a pummelling of the body and a form of physical therapy.

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go inside the weapon

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club

indicators.note: the word bar is wrecked, its letters smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A pub is smashed up in a nightclub, a grisly scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a nightclub in the surface but is the heavy weapon; 'wrecked' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ghastly and deathly, grisly in tone, fits both words.

clue.text: Naive curiosity as to what money may earn?

parts.note: simple means naive or unsophisticated
interest means curiosity

explanation.surface: An innocent person wonders what savings might bring in.
explanation.definitionFit: Return paid on a principal sum alone, without compounding, is what a deposit may yield.

clue.text: This author is no one we know

definitions.text: This author is no one we know

parts.words: This author is no one we know
parts.note: a writer whose identity is unknown, credited by the short label printed under unattributed verse

explanation.surface: A mysterious writer is unknown to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Unattributed verse and quotations are credited to an unknown writer with an abbreviated label meaning nameless.

clue.text: Go off and walk slowly into river

indicators.note: the plodding is put into the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
to plod is to walk slowly and heavily

explanation.surface: Someone sets off and wades slowly into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb going off blows up, bursting violently.

clue.text: Get by with no degree of honour

definitions.meaning: to scrape through or manage adequately
an ordinary university result awarded without honours

explanation.surface: A student scrapes through university without distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a degree given without honours is called by this name, below a third-class honours result.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape through is to succeed narrowly, and a British ordinary degree is awarded with no honours class.

clue.text: A pint is poured for entertainer

indicators.note: a pint being poured spills its letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A pint is poured for a pub performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard player performing to an audience is an entertainer.

clue.text: Measure dogs, perhaps, that are picked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: dogs are an example of pets

explanation.surface: Someone measures dogs that have been lifted up.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a measure or action taken towards an end.

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An American led a group out without hiding anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something openly, bare and unhidden, is doing it without concealment.

parts.note: combine harvesters suggests farm machines, but read as a Soviet combine of harvesters it is a state-run agricultural cooperative

explanation.surface: Someone talks about Soviet farm machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A kolkhoz was a Soviet cooperative where land and labour were pooled.

clue.text: Ordinary volume, but it contains interesting snippets

parts.note: something ordinary is commonplace, everyday
a volume is a book

explanation.surface: A dull-looking tome turns out to be full of gems.
explanation.definitionFit: A notebook of collected quotations and extracts is kept by readers to record memorable passages.

definitions.meaning: a formal social gathering for dancing

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a circle dance is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a round thing, and a grand evening party with dancing shares the same name.

annotationWithheld.why: Canned beef that is poisonous (5): T(OX)IN, where 'Canned' must give TIN and also signal the insertion of OX, one word doing two jobs

parts.note: to have led is to have gone in front

explanation.surface: A boy leads the way down the slope on his sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge for sliding down snow, in American usage, is the same thing as a toboggan.

parts.note: an oven is a cooker

explanation.surface: Women at the stove cooperated.
explanation.definitionFit: Threads interlaced on a loom have been plaited or worked together.

indicators.note: the row goes round the letter for good

parts.note: a tier is a row, as in seats

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over a good cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A striped big cat of Asia is one of the large felines.

clue.text: Summary of one book on record

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral one
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A précis of a single book appears on a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A condensed abstract of a work, an essence in brief, is an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Two shortly feeling irritable and nervous

indicators.note: the word Two is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: itchy means restless or irritable

explanation.surface: Two people feel cross and jumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being jumpy and on edge is the same as being jittery.

definitions.meaning: oven-ready birds are sold with their innards removed

explanation.surface: Cowardice is likened to supermarket poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chickens' suggests cowardice, but the second definition is literal: sold without innards.
explanation.definitionFit: A coward lacks nerve or guts, and a cleaned bird has had its entrails removed.

clue.text: Sort of car robbers need? That's ridiculous!

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that robbers need a particular car.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves escape in a fast vehicle, and 'you're joking!' is the British cry of disbelief.

indicators.note: curtailed means its tail is cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a swan song is a last performance

explanation.surface: A star's farewell performance was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloria Swanson was a Hollywood silent-film star.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress of Sunset Boulevard is identified by her first name.

clue.text: Suspecting there's a charge to fish

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone suspects there is a fee for fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a hunch or suspicion that something is so is a sense of intuiting it.

clue.text: Old robber, needing something to eat, horribly apt to break in

indicators.note: the scrambled letters break into the word for food

parts.note: food is something to eat

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: A hungry highwayman is ready to burgle a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' turns APT into TPA, which breaks 'in' to FOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A highwayman who robbed travellers on foot is an archaic term for a thief.

parts.note: a gent is a chap, a man

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up turns the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: lee is a sheltered side, out of the wind

explanation.surface: A refined man had a protected childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite and refined, of good family, is the sense of well-mannered breeding.

definitions.meaning: a word or expression used for something
one of the divisions of the academic year

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a school period is called.
explanation.definitionFit: A word for something is its expression, and the school year divides into three of these sessions.

annotationWithheld.why: Lord's storehouse empty? (5): BAR(O)N, where 'empty' must give O and also signal its insertion into BARN, one word doing two jobs

definitions.meaning: to incline or be disposed towards

explanation.surface: Someone is inclined towards slimness.
explanation.definitionFit: To incline towards something is to favour it, and slim meat or a slender body has little fat.

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a meal
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone earns cash discreetly.
explanation.walkthrough: DOSH is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: It is informal slang for cash.

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: a crock is an old, worn-out or disabled person

explanation.surface: A dangerous animal is nearly lame.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocodile, shortened informally, is a dangerous reptile.

clue.text: Having mounted fine horse, following direction for town

indicators.note: the rest of the pieces come after the direction

parts.note: west is a compass direction
on, as in sitting on a horse once mounted
super means excellent, fine
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A rider mounts a fine horse and heads west to town.
explanation.walkthrough: WESTON-SUPER-MARE is a seaside town in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an English seaside resort on the Bristol Channel, a place rather than a city.

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A church has a popular attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaw's front point is one of the facial features.

clue.text: Claimed to be convertible, like our currency

indicators.note: convertible means able to be changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone claims a currency can be exchanged freely.
explanation.walkthrough: British money went to a base-ten system in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Pounds and pence are divided in tens and hundreds, a base-ten system.
